CVE-2026-116127.title: Starlet versions before 0.33 for Perl send a body in responses to HEAD requests, corrupting the next response on a persistent or pipelined connection
CVE-2026-116127.description:
Starlet versions before 0.33 for Perl send a body in responses to HEAD requests, corrupting the next response on a persistent or pipelined connection.

The request method is not passed to the response writer, so whatever body the application returns for a HEAD request is sent. With Plack::Middleware::Head the body is empty, but an HTTP/1.1 response without a Content-Length header still gets the chunked encoding terminator. Responses with status 204 or 304 are also sent with their body.

Pipelined GET and HEAD requests keep the connection open even when keep-alive is disabled, which is the default. A client or proxy reading the connection takes the extra bytes as the start of the next response, which may desynchronize a proxy that shares the connection across clients.

CVE-2026-127138.title: Circumvention of offline barcode revocation check in pretixSCAN
CVE-2026-127138.description:
pretix provides a mechanism where ticket QR codes are cryptographically signed and can be verified by our pretixSCAN apps in offline mode without any database of valid tickets. pretixSCAN checks the signature to verify that the ticket was issued by the correct pretix event and compares the QR code against a list of revoked QR codes. A QR code becomes revoked when the order is canceled, or the ticket is changed in a way that a new QR code needs to be generated.

However, the parsing of the QR code in all of our pretixSCAN apps contained a faulty computation, rendering the check for the correct length of the contents faulty. This way, an attacker is able to craft multiple QR codes for the same ticket which have the same content, but look different and therefore do not match against the revocation list. This does not allow to fabricate entirely new tickets, but it does allow to enter the event with e.g. a canceled ticket. This attack requires pretixSCAN to be scanning in offline mode…

CVE-2026-45355.title: Netatalk: Integer Underflow in Spotlight RPC String Length Calculation (sl_unpack_cpx)
CVE-2026-45355.description: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, the afpd Spotlight RPC string unmarshalling path in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c uses sl_unpack_cpx to calculate slen from qlen and the attacker-controlled used_in_last_block value without preventing a negative result. An authenticated AFP client can send a complex string or UTF-16 string element that makes slen negative, and the implicit conversion to size_t causes dalloc_strndup or convert_string_allocate to read beyond the heap buffer. The out-of-bounds read can expose heap data through the RPC response or crash the worker process. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

CVE-2026-99509.title: media: imon: fix use-after-free in display_close via dev_dbg
CVE-2026-99509.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: imon: fix use-after-free in display_close via dev_dbg

ictx->dev is a raw pointer to the usb_interface's embedded device.
On disconnect, usb_disconnect() can drop the last reference on the
interface and free it while a userspace fd for /dev/lcd0 is still
open. When that fd is later closed, display_close() dereferences
the now-freed ictx->dev via dev_dbg(), causing a use-after-free.

Remove the dev_dbg() calls that dereference ictx->dev in
display_close() and free_imon_context(), rather than taking a
reference on the device.
